question: Which parts of tezgah's harness are measurably load-bearing, which are dead weight or unstable, and what change to the harness improves a named metric without breaking a measured invariant?

evaluation.metric: for each harness component: (a) refusals per rule over the whole ledger corpus, (b) injected bytes per event against that event's budget, (c) wall-clock ms per gated call (process) and per decision (in-process), (d) per-rule host parity (implemented/absent/divergent)
evaluation.baseline: the repository's own recorded numbers where they exist: the pre-tool path at 50.965 ms (docs/gate.md), the subagent budget at 4400 B (hooks/tezgah_context.py:687), the arm-bench lab's pooled harness delta 40/50 against 40/50 (benchmarks/lab README)
evaluation.locked_at: 2026-09-20T16:05:00+0300 (state.json written after the first four result sets; the per-experiment thresholds they are read against were committed in e1dda58 BEFORE any run - experiments/E*/protocol.md - and this deviation is recorded in log.md)

hypotheses.verdict: holds: session_start 76.2% of 12000 B, user_prompt 18.9% of 6000 B, subagent_start 91.5% of 4400 B; the live half does not grow with the repository
hypotheses.text: the always-on injection stays under its budget in a normal session, and subagent_start is the event that binds

hypotheses.verdict: holds: explorer and order at zero in 1613 ledgers; task, race and lang confined to one day each
hypotheses.text: at least one shipped deny rule has never refused a real call, and at least two fired only on the day they shipped

hypotheses.verdict: holds: decision p50 0.43 ms, unchanged at 20x the corpus; the gated call costs 61.0 ms, all of it interpreter start plus import
hypotheses.text: the gate decision is cheap in process and does not grow with the corpus, and what a host pays per call is module import rather than rules

hypotheses.verdict: holds with one half scoped to the tree it was read on: lang was absent from the plugin then and is enforced by delegation now (C26); five labels stay divergent, five of fourteen are compared by the plugin suite, and delegation still fails open by design
hypotheses.text: the opencode mirror is missing or diverges on rules the Python gate enforces, and its delegation fails open

hypotheses.verdict: re-taken by E5b (C27) on 2026-09-22: the guarded half holds (the guard at all seven entry points, the plugin's core asks all through one collect with a deadline) and the bounded half failed only at the Stop path, which was then bounded through turn_rows; H5 stays refuted on the two reads unbounded by construction, used() and _hash_file, which no run has timed.
hypotheses.text: every hot-path operation is guarded and bounded
